source.title: Jailbreak to Protect: Buffering and Reinforcing via Temporary Jailbreaking for Safe Fine-Tuning in Large Language Models
source.authors: Seokil Ham; Jaehyuk Jang; Wonjun Lee; Changick Kim

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports harmful-output scores after standard fine-tuning across harmful-data ratios, dataset sizes, tasks, and models. This bears on fine-tuning safety degradation, but uses its own evaluation setup rather than reproducing the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The SFT harmful-score results are included because they report model outcomes after fine-tuning. The paper's BufferLoRA results and temporary-jailbreaking procedure are intentionally induced behavior, so they are not treated as evidence that safety degrades without that inducement. The gradient analysis is recorded under fits_no_version; it does not measure first-token KL concentration, compliant-opening bypasses, or safety localization in a small set of parameters. Results for other defense methods are omitted because they do not measure the claim's object independently of the SFT comparisons.
record.test_reason: The paper's undefended SFT baseline reports Harmful Scores (Beaver-Dam-7B on the BeaverTails test set) after fine-tuning on benign-only data (p=0) and on benign data mixed with 50–1,000 harmful examples. Table A6 gives the un-fine-tuned LLaMA3-8B-Instruct score (19.2), so the safety change from fine-tuning can be read. The defense method and the gradient analysis do not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that temporary jailbreaking via BufferLoRA saturates safety-degrading gradients while preserving benign-task gradients. Combined with ReinforceLoRA and QR-based merging, it keeps the Harmful Score low and Fine-tuning Accuracy high across harmful ratios, data sizes, tasks and models. They also note that standard fine-tuning degrades safety even on benign data.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes a defensive pipeline with a harmful-behavior BufferLoRA, user fine-tuning, and a refusal-trained ReinforceLoRA; it does not reproduce the original fine-tuning or first-token analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to harmful-data ratio, user-data size, task, model architecture, BufferLoRA and ReinforceLoRA training-data size, and QR projection strength. It also notes that the temporary-jailbreak effect depends on sufficiently strong BufferLoRA training.

fits_no_version.finding: For the safety-aligned checkpoint, the Safety Gradient Score is negative on both harmful and harmless data. A jailbroken checkpoint scores near zero on both, with comparable gradient norms on harmless data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporary harmful-behavior activation saturates safety-degrading gradients while keeping gradients useful for benign-task learning.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The SFT tables do not provide a no-fine-tuning harmful-score baseline. Harmful Score is defined through a classifier rather than as a direct refusal rate. The gradient evidence is presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The authors state that experiments cover models in the 4B-13B range and do not verify frontier-scale models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the row limit. Other defense-method results, framework ablations, and intentionally induced BufferLoRA behavior are not included because they do not independently test the claim's stated fine-tuning or bypass behaviors.

untested.parts: Very few harmful examples (fewer than 50); a direct refusal-rate measure.
Carefully chosen or selected benign data; only ordinary task data (GSM8K) is tested, and only on LLaMA3-8B-Instruct.
Whole version. GCG, PAIR and TAP are run only on already fine-tuned models (Table A7).

missing.what: Base (un-fine-tuned) Harmful Scores: LLaMA3-8B-Instruct 19.2, LLaMA3-8B-ReFAT 16.2, LLaMA2-13B-Chat 6.4.
SFT at default p=0.1: LLaMA3-8B-LAT 74.0, LLaMA3-8B-ReFAT 74.0 (base 16.2), LLaMA2-13B-Chat 33.2 (base 6.4). The 13B rise is large but its absolute level is much lower.
Benign-only SFT Harmful Score on GSM8K: 32.6 (n=1000), 28.2 (n=5000), 30.8 (n=7000).

record.verdict_notes: The record wrongly states that no pre-fine-tuning baseline is reported; Table A6 gives one. Tables 2–4 use the default harmful ratio p=0.1 stated in Section 6, so those rows bear on V1, not V2. Harmful Score is classifier-judged, not a refusal rate.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fine-tuning on only a few examples. The reported harmful-score measure is not a direct refusal rate, and the main tables do not report a no-fine-tuning harmful-score baseline.

The paper reports harmful scores after benign-only fine-tuning, but does not report the same model's harmful score before fine-tuning, so the increase attributable to benign fine-tuning cannot be determined.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Whether training data or objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens and its robustness.
